beats.headline: Stocks post worst day since April as Fed holds rates and Mideast tensions flare
beats.body: The Dow fell 1,153 points (-2.19%) to 51,594.14, the S&P 500 dropped 1.52% to 7,316.15, and the Nasdaq slid 1.74% to 24,442.94 on Wednesday after the Fed held interest rates steady and struck a hawkish tone; oil prices also rose on renewed Middle East tensions.

beats.headline: Iran fires missiles at US forces in Jordan; Trump orders retaliatory strikes
beats.body: Iran launched a barrage of ballistic missiles at a US base and CENTCOM facility in Jordan Wednesday night, all of which were intercepted; President Trump said it was America's turn to respond, and US forces carried out retaliatory strikes into early Thursday.

beats.headline: China tightens patrols around Taiwan as US carrier group works the South China Sea
beats.body: Chinese coast guard and civilian vessels expanded patrols in waters east of Taiwan through July, stoking concern in Washington that Beijing is rehearsing a blockade-style containment strategy, while the USS George Washington carrier strike group continues freedom-of-navigation patrols in the contested South China Sea.

beats.headline: US and Saudi jets strike Iran-backed militias in Iraq as death toll climbs
beats.body: US and Saudi fighter aircraft struck Iran-backed militia sites across seven Iraqi provinces this week, killing at least 20 fighters in the first joint US-Saudi strikes of the conflict; the US military death toll in the broader campaign stands at 18 since late February.

beats.headline: Pentagon clears $76.6B multiyear submarine deal with General Dynamics and HII
beats.body: The Pentagon completed statutory certification allowing the Navy to negotiate a multiyear contract for nine Block VI Virginia-class attack submarines and five Columbia-class boats, a deal projected to save $2.4 billion versus buying hulls year to year and to stabilize the submarine industrial base.

beats.headline: Over 1,100 AI staffers, including Anthropic scientists, ask US to build an AI 'slowdown' toolkit
beats.body: More than 1,100 employees at OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta, including chief scientists, signed a letter urging Washington to build the technical and governance tools for a verifiable international slowdown of AI development if capabilities ever outpace safe oversight; the letter stops short of calling for an immediate pause.

beats.headline: Bears open camp with Sweat back, Gordon and Edwards sidelined
beats.body: The Bears opened training camp practices in Lake Forest with DE Montez Sweat activated off the non-football illness list, while CB Kyler Gordon (calf) and LB T.J. Edwards (calf) remain out; QB Caleb Williams drew praise for early growth under new OC Ben Johnson.

beats.headline: Liberty University returns as Byron's primary sponsor for Brickyard weekend
beats.body: Liberty University served as the primary sponsor on William Byron's No. 24 Hendrick Motorsports Chevrolet for the Cup Series' Brickyard 400 weekend at Indianapolis Motor Speedway.

beats.headline: PCA mourns Paul Kooistra, longtime Covenant Seminary president and MTW leader
beats.body: Dr. Paul D. Kooistra, 83, died July 1 after a battle with cancer; he served as president of Covenant Theological Seminary from 1985 and later as coordinator of Mission to the World, which grew under his leadership into the largest missionary-sending agency in Presbyterian history.
